item.title: US War With Iran Hits Six Month Mark | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/28/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments on interest rates were the “least interesting” part of his Jackson Hole speech and points instead to his focus on the availability of credit. Democratic Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts discusses her bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which aims to create federal oversight of the most advanced AI models through reporting, independent audits, and emergency safeguards. Sec. Leon Panetta, former US Secretary of Defense, says the US is “now trapped in another forever war” with Iran after six months of fighting with “no end in sight.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sec. Panetta: US Is Trapped In Another Forever War
item.description: Sec. Leon Panetta, former US Secretary of Defense, says the US is “now trapped in another forever war” with Iran after six months of fighting with “no end in sight.” Panetta says Iran is essentially holding the US economy hostage through its control of the Strait of Hormuz and argues President Trump needs to find a way to open the critical waterway. He says US efforts to clear mines have not taken away Iran’s leverage as Tehran continues to threaten ships and use missiles to restrict traffic through the strait. Panetta says there is “no way to take control of this war” as long as Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Trahan: Federal AI Governance Is 'Missing'
item.description: Democratic Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts discusses her bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which aims to create federal oversight of the most advanced AI models through reporting, independent audits and emergency safeguards.. Rep. Trahan calls criticism that the bill would broadly preempt state laws "completely false," arguing instead it creates a "narrow federal lane" while preserving state authority in areas including privacy and consumer protection. She also calls for hearings with leading AI companies and broader bipartisan action on data centers, workers, and AI in schools. She speaks with Tyler Kendall and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Set to Take Control of Major Portion of Venezuelan Oil Wealth
item.description: The US is set to take majority control over a huge amount of Venezuela’s oil wealth in an unprecedented maneuver that officials said would create the world’s second-largest private oil company by reserves and secure American petroleum supplies for decades to come.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Eric Martin

item.title: Duppler: Warsh’s Credit Message Mattered More Than Rates
item.description: Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments on interest rates were the “least interesting” part of his Jackson Hole speech and points instead to his focus on the availability of credit. Duppler says Warsh offered confidence to markets about credit and liquidity, arguing that message takes on added importance as federal debt tops $40 trillion and the AI buildout creates significant capital needs. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon in Talks With Venezuelan Mogul on Oil Deal
item.description: The Pentagon is discussing an arrangement with Venezuelan mogul Alejandro Betancourt as part of a broader push tied to President Trump's goal of tapping Venezuela's large oil reserves. The reported deal would aim to help jump-start Venezuelan production, which has improved somewhat but remains constrained by caution from companies considering returning to the country. Eric Martin has exclusive reporting on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump to Discuss High Fuel Prices With Oil Refiners Next Week
item.description: President Donald Trump is set to meet with US oil refining executives as he confronts persistently high gasoline prices stoked by the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Elizabeth Elkin, Cole Martin and Nathan Risser

item.title: Trump Assails NY’s Hochul After She Rejects ‘Lake America’ Name
item.description: President Donald Trump hit back at New York Governor Kathy Hochul after she said her state wouldn’t use “Lake America,” the administration’s new name for Lake Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Jeff Mason

item.title: ICE Arrests Right-Wing Provocateur, Influencer Milo Yiannopoulos
item.description: Federal immigration authorities arrested right-wing provocateur and online influencer Milo Yiannopoulos at an airport in Louisiana after he was accused of overstaying his visa.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Ecuador Court Convicts Former President Moreno of Taking Bribes
item.description: Three judges in Ecuador found former President Lenín Moreno guilty of accepting bribes from China’s Sinohydro Corp. Ltd. when he was vice president in 2010, according to a unanimous verdict.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Kueffner

item.title: Warsh's Jackson Hole Inflation Vow | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/28/2026
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh warned inflation isn’t meaningfully slowing, but vowed policymakers will return inflation to their 2% goal. Bloomberg News' Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee is in Jackson Hole where Warsh gave his first speech since becoming chairman of the Central Bank. Brooke May, Managing Partner at Evans May Wealth, also reacts to Warsh's inflation vow with some skepticism. Then, Linamar Executive Chair Linda Hasenfratz discusses President Trump's tariff threats on the Canadian cars and auto parts, saying if a 50% tariff is imposed by next year it would bring the industry "to its knees." Finally, Affirm Founder & CEO Max Levchin explains how his company sets rates and keeps up with a growing industry, arguing Affirm's transparency makes it stand out from competitors. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Debt Reckoning and Trump’s Post-Midterm Playbook Come Into Focus
item.description: What we can expect to see from the White House and Congress.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Pentagon in Talks With Venezuelan Mogul for Massive Oil Deal
item.description: The US government is pursuing a major stake in Venezuelan oil reserves via a potential partnership between the Department of Defense and Alejandro Betancourt, a controversial energy investor who has become a key middleman between the two countries.
item.dc:creator: Ben Bartenstein, Peter Millard and Eric Martin

item.title: US Postal Service Appeals Order Halting Mail-in Ballot Curbs
item.description: The Trump administration is appealing a judge’s order halting new US Postal Service restrictions on mail-in ballots, moving quickly to reinstate the challenged rules after they were paused in a high-stakes clash that could shape the November midterms and the fight to control Congress.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr and Zoe Tillman

item.title: Warsh Says Inflation Isn’t Slowing | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/28/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall discuss Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech in Jackson Hole. On today's show, Austrian National Bank Governor Martin Kocher, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Retired US Army Brigadier General Leela Gray. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Newsom Blocked on Shielding Utilities From Fire Liabilities
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom’s push to shield publicly traded utilities from some wildfire liabilities has been blocked by state lawmakers, according to people familiar with the negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford and Michelle Ma

item.title: Why the US Wants a Stake in Venezuela’s Oil
item.description: While Venezuela isn’t the powerhouse oil producer it used to be, the country nonetheless has some of the world’s largest oil reserves. Since the US seized then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro on Jan. 3, the US has restored diplomatic ties and is working with interim President Delcy Rodríguez’s government in Caracas. item.title: DOJ Balks at Demands for Details on Trump’s Deal in IRS Case
item.description: The US Justice Department is pushing back on requests for information about how it resolved President Donald Trump’s $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, accusing challengers of the deal of improperly using the courts to pry loose details they aren’t entitled to receive.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Anthropic Scores Legal Win Against Trump Administration
item.description: A US judge ordered the Trump administration to lift its ban on Anthropic’s AI technology for federal agencies, finding the restriction wasn’t adequately justified and was partly intended to make a public example of the company. Bloomberg’s Rachel Metz explains why the ruling doesn’t immediately end Anthropic’s legal fight. She also breaks down a separate warning from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other companies about the growing threat of AI-enabled cyberattacks with Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Announces Plan to Let Ranchers Process Their Own Food
item.description: President Donald Trump said he plans to authorize farmers and ranchers to process their own food, the administration’s latest move targeting US meatpackers in an effort to bring down high beef prices.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian
